title: Kick ‘em while he’s down
subtitle: wtf guys
html:
In my last installment, I documented my upgrade from waffling new-grad to waffling research fellow sleeping on an air mattress in South Boston.

Today?

I have a bed!

Huzzah!

I’m also no longer a research fellow.

Huzzah?

The org structure where I was doing my fellowship is a little goofy. I learned about two weeks before my fellowship ended that the team I had been with for the past four months wasn’t looking to hire, and the team that was looking to hire wasn’t sure about me because they hadn’t worked with me much during my fellowship. That is fair, I suppose, but considering that I had been telling every Tom, Dick, and Harry at the org that I need a job, this would have been nice to know sooner. Or, ya know, it might have been nice of them to take a look at the guy who says he desperately needs a job if you are looking to hire. Anywho…

I poked and prodded, and now the team looking to hire is letting me work with them as a contractor for the rest of the year. I’ll be finishing my fellowship projects and attempting to convince the org to hire me. It’s like a long-term work trial with no benefits or reassurance. Totally not unsettling at all, right?.

So now I devote most of my time to contracting stuff, but I’m also attempting to make time to lift, teach myself computational biology, and train enough jiu-jitsu to stay above the sanity poverty line. I think I was managing it all somewhat well until my knee went kaboom at jiu-jitsu last Thursday. Like, wtf, world? You had to kick a man while he’s down?

I’m not mad, just disappointed.

*Okay, maybe a little mad.

Next thing I knew, I was flying back to Minnesota because #idonthavemassachussettshealthinsuranceyet. I need an MRI. And I suspect partial ACL and meniscus tears, but we’ll have to wait and see. The pop was loud. Let’s hope it’s not surgical. I’ve had enough surgeries for a while.

There are always silver linings in the piles of turds we walk through, though. But those are for me to know and for you to wonder about. The tone here isn’t meant to be mushy gratefulness; it’s snark! Like, wtf, guys?! What is happening?!

At least this is all temporary. Contracting purgatory ends December 31st—with or without a job—and my knee will either heal on its own or through surgery. The bad news is that I’m now dangling from the sanity poverty line. My pinky and ring finger already slipped off, and my hands freaking hurt. But hey, that’s life, ya know? Builds character.

I’m trying, guys.

I’m trying.

Talk soon,

Charlie
